What are the risk factors for necrotising enterocolitis (NEC)?
Prematurity, formula feeds, a fast increase in feeds, asphyxia, polycythaemia and a patent ductus arteriosus.
What are the clinical features of NEC?
Feed intolerance, bilious vomiting, abdominal distension, bloody stools and shock.
What is the typical X-ray sign of NEC?

How does symmetrical intrauterine growth restriction differ from asymmetrical?

Symmetrical growth restriction starts early and all measurements are small (chromosomal disorders, congenital infections). Asymmetrical growth restriction starts late and the head is spared (placental cause).
Which type of intrauterine growth restriction has the better prognosis?
Asymmetrical growth restriction, because the head is spared.
What are the problems of a baby who is small for gestational age?
Hypoglycaemia, hypothermia, polycythaemia, asphyxia and hypocalcaemia.
What is the main cause of babies who are large for gestational age?
Maternal diabetes. Other causes are large parents and Beckwith–Wiedemann syndrome.
What are the features of a post-term baby?
